concerns.text: Tasks T069 (Pauling structural constraints) and T070 (Solvent/Hydration model) are present in the task list but have no corresponding User Story, Acceptance Criteria, or plan section in spec.md or plan.md. These tasks implement unapproved scope that contradicts the 'Resource-Bound Execution' principle (Constitution Principle VII) and the defined MVP scope.

Tasks T071 (Standard of Evidence) and T072 (Resource Budget/FLOPs) are present but lack corresponding User Stories or Acceptance Criteria in spec.md. The spec defines US2 acceptance via t-test and MAE thresholds, not via explicit documentation of experimental instruments or FLOP accounting. These tasks represent unapproved scope creep.

Tasks T073 (Approximation Error Model), T074 (Path Integral Visualizer), and T075 (Observable Mapping) are present but have no corresponding User Story or Acceptance Criteria in spec.md. US3 focuses on feature importance and sensitivity sweeps, not on modeling 'missing degrees of freedom' or generating Feynman diagrams. These are unapproved scope additions.

Tasks T076 (Physical Model Discipline) and T077 (Ontological Status) require synthesizing documentation based on reviewer personas (Pauling, Franklin, Feynman, Einstein) that are not authorized in spec.md or plan.md. The spec Constraints and Plan Risk Management do not mandate these specific deliverables, creating a disconnect between authorized scope and required tasks.

Task T019 (Implement export_geometries.py) is listed as a separate task in Phase 3, but the spec.md US1 Acceptance Criteria explicitly states 'Optimized geometries exported to XYZ format' as part of the US1 goal. While T013 mentions exporting, T019 duplicates this requirement as a standalone task without a clear distinct scope or dependency separation from T013, potentially fragmenting the US1 implementation.

Task T069 references 'Linus Pauling reviews' and 'Rosalind Franklin reviews' in its description. These persona names and specific review references are not part of the spec.md or plan.md artifacts and should be removed to maintain traceability to the actual specification requirements rather than external commentary.
